name: Dividend quality investing
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Reliable Dividend Income
caseLead: Companies with dividends supported by free cash flow can provide relatively reliable income and increase payouts as earnings grow. The opportunity persists because many investors chase headline yield without checking cash flow, which leaves companies with covered and growing payouts priced like the average company, while tax changes, bank payout limits and tariffs keep altering which payouts are safe.
caseRest: A fall in share prices can exceed the dividends collected because dividend-paying stocks remain exposed to equity market risk. Dividends are cut in recessions when profits fall, as in March 2020 when many companies suspended payments to preserve cash. Higher bond yields also reduce the appeal of dividend income, so rate-sensitive holdings such as utilities can fall even when earnings are stable.
figNote: Each card shows the change in the S&P 500 over the episode, measured from its high before the event to its low, or from its low to its high in a rally. It is a simple measure of how severe the move in the equity market was, so readers can compare how a dividend portfolio behaved against it.

events.title: US downgrade drives a defensive rotation
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 19% from April to October 2011 after the US credit rating downgrade and the euro area debt crisis. Results were mixed because covered dividends held up and drew defensive buying, but share prices still fell.

events.title: Taper signal lifts yields and hits dividend shares
events.text: The Federal Reserve signalled in May 2013 that it would slow bond purchases, and the S&P 500 fell about 6% in the following month. The strategy lost because higher bond yields made dividend income less attractive, especially for utilities.

events.title: Tighter policy and trade tension weigh on equities
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 20% from September to December 2018 as the Federal Reserve raised rates and US-China tariffs weighed on growth. Results were mixed because dividend payers fell less than the index but still lost value.

events.title: Covid lockdowns force dividend cuts
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 34% in five weeks to 23 March 2020, and many companies cut dividends to preserve cash. The strategy lost because dividend cuts reduced income and share prices fell with the market.

events.title: Vaccine news revives cyclical dividend shares
events.text: The S&P 500 rose about 11% in November 2020 after the first effective Covid vaccine results, and investors moved into energy, banks and industrial companies. The strategy gained because dividend payers in these sectors recovered as earnings expectations improved.

events.title: US tariffs trigger a sharp equity sell-off
events.text: The S&P 500 fell about 19% from February to 8 April 2025 as sweeping US tariffs raised the risk of weaker earnings. Results were mixed because dividend payers fell less than the index, but companies with imported inputs faced margin pressure.

instrument: Global large-cap shares; reviewed twice a year; dividends reinvested
rules: Companies selected on dividend cover, balance sheet strength and five-year dividend growth; yields above the 90th percentile excluded to avoid unsustainable payouts
costs: Estimated commissions, bid-ask spreads and withholding tax on dividends
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from covered dividends to drawdown control

legs.position: Dividend payers with cash cover above 1.5 times, 40 stocks
legs.purpose: Earns dividend income and earnings growth

legs.position: Dividend growers with 10 years of increases
legs.purpose: Adds income that grows with inflation

legs.position: Put options, 3 months, 10% out of the money
legs.purpose: Limits losses in a market sell-off
Holds cash for rebalancing and earns the cash rate

entry: Free cash flow covers the dividend at least 1.5 times
size: No stock above 4% and no sector above 20%
exit: Position closed after a dividend cut, or when cover falls below 1.2 times
stop: Equity weight cut by a third if the S&P 500 falls 20% from its high
marketWatch: Rehyn monitors dividend cover, net debt against earnings and the gap between dividend yields and government bond yields, because these show whether payouts are safe and attractive. Corporate earnings seasons, central bank rate decisions and changes to dividend tax or bank payout rules are the events that matter most. A rise in bond yields would weigh on rate-sensitive payers, while weak earnings would put the weakest payouts at risk.

favourable.heading: Defensive rotations in sell-offs
favourable.text: Defensive rotations favour the strategy because investors move into companies with steady cash flow and covered dividends when growth expectations fall. In 2022 the S&P 500 fell about 18% while dividend-focused funds lost far less, because earnings visible today were valued above growth expected years ahead.

favourable.heading: Rising corporate cash flow
favourable.text: Rising free cash flow favours the strategy because companies can raise dividends without borrowing, which lifts both income and share prices. From 2010 to 2019 S&P 500 dividends per share more than doubled as earnings grew.

favourable.heading: Stable or falling bond yields
favourable.text: Stable bond yields favour the strategy because dividend income stays attractive against government bonds, so valuations of dividend payers hold. In 2019 the 10-year Treasury yield fell from about 2.7% to 1.9%, and dividend payers gained alongside the market.

adverse.heading: Recessions that force dividend cuts
adverse.text: Recessions hurt the strategy because falling profits make companies cut payouts, which lowers income and weakens share prices together. In March 2020 companies in energy, banking and airlines suspended or cut dividends, which caused large losses for portfolios that held them.

adverse.heading: Rising bond yields
adverse.text: Rising bond yields hurt the strategy because investors can earn similar income from government bonds, which lowers the valuation of dividend shares. In May and June 2013 the 10-year Treasury yield rose by nearly 1 percentage point and US utilities fell about 10%.

adverse.heading: Tax and regulatory limits on payouts
adverse.text: Regulatory limits hurt the strategy when authorities restrict dividends to protect capital in a crisis. In 2020 European and British regulators asked banks to suspend dividends, which removed a large share of income from regional dividend benchmarks.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each figure includes the dividends received during the event window.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in global share prices, bond yields and sector returns, which are then applied to the strategy's current holdings, including the index put options.
